business_problem: Longbow Advantage needed a scalable way to replace spreadsheet-based warehouse reporting with real-time visibility across high-volume supply-chain operations.
solution_summary: Longbow Advantage built its Rebus warehouse-visibility platform on MongoDB Atlas running on Google Cloud to give customers one near-real-time view of complex supply-chain operations. Rebus ingests data in many formats from warehouse systems and related applications, then stores it in Atlas so performance reporting, yard operations, labor management, and downstream business lines can be analyzed together. The document database model was a strong fit because clients generate massive warehouse event volumes and need to correlate them quickly without the delay of monolithic spreadsheets or fragile backup tooling. Atlas also removed the burden of self-managing large clusters, providing point-in-time recovery, rapid snapshot restores, and on-demand scaling for 10TB-plus environments. This architecture turns raw operational events into warehouse intelligence that manufacturers, retailers, and distributors can use to make decisions faster, reduce labor and service costs, and keep goods moving under changing market conditions.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores and serves Rebus warehouse data so Longbow can deliver real-time visibility, reporting, and labor-management insights.

data_flow: Operational data from warehouse systems and other supply-chain platforms is ingested into MongoDB Atlas, organized for fast access inside Rebus, and surfaced back as real-time visibility, reporting, and optimization insights for warehouse, yard, and labor operations.
business_outcome: Rebus helped customers automate warehouse reporting, accelerate decisions, reduce labor costs by 9%, improve cost to serve by 21%, deliver over $1 million in annual savings, and return some algorithms in 20 seconds instead of timing out after 10 minutes.
metrics: Rebus currently manages 10 terabytes of uncompressed data every week.
A major pharmaceutical distributor reduced labor cost by 9%, improved cost to serve by 21%, and realized more than $1 million in annual savings, with an ongoing ROI of 13X.
